text: It was difficult to contact them by phone, and it's the same at every branch. The after-sales service is poor, and they don't provide clear details. We decided to have a scaling and filling removal/replacement done on December 12th, 2025. Immediately after the procedure, we experienced pain in the area where the local anesthetic was injected, even after the anesthetic wore off. We waited, thinking it might gradually subside, but by the second day, the pain hadn't improved. We tried to contact the branch again and informed the administrator about the symptoms, requesting an immediate examination. However, the administrator told us we had to wait 8-9 days for an available appointment with the doctor who performed the procedure. We asked if another doctor could see us, as the 8-9 day wait was very long and we were extremely concerned, having never experienced this before after dental work. The administrator then said we would have to go to another branch, which was inconvenient for us due to the long travel time and our work commitments. This was why we initially chose this branch – for its convenience. After explaining the situation, the administrator agreed to let us return to the original branch for an appointment. They didn't mention any additional charges, but after the examination, the clinic informed us that... There was an additional charge of 200 baht for the examination because I was examined by a different doctor. While 200 baht isn't a big issue for us, the negative experience was the poor service, the lack of understanding of our concerns during after-sales support, the unfriendly demeanor and attitude of the clinic's administrator, and the complete lack of prior notification about the additional charges. These are the things customers expect from a healthcare provider. In short, this will be my first and last time at this clinic. I would absolutely not recommend this clinic to anyone.

restaurant_name: คลินิกทันตกรรม Smile Seasons ท่าพระ
text:
I've never written a review and given such low ratings before. I was very disappointed. Previously, I was impressed with the excellent service and skilled dentist. I was another one of those difficult orthodontic cases. I'd been to several places, and they recommended Mahidol or Chulalongkorn. I saw the newly opened Tha Phra branch, so I went for an evaluation. The dentist said it was possible, so I did. I spent a lot of money there over the four years I had braces, over 100,000 baht.

The first two years were impressive. The dentist kept updating me on my teeth, telling me how they were doing, how much time they'd left, and what they were doing. Later, I started to feel like they were dragging me out and my teeth weren't changing much, so I asked about the treatment plan. The dentist was stunned for a moment, then called me into another room and continued with the treatment plan. It was very abrupt. They wanted me to get a dental implant, which they hadn't said anything about before. They just dragged me out and changed the rubber bands. I told them to hold off on it because the cost was too high, and I wasn't ready yet.

After that, the dentist changed completely. He used to be a completely different person. He was always busy updating me on my teeth, but he didn't talk to me. He was always busy with other appointments. He only had a few minutes to change the rubber bands, so I moved on to another case. This happened every time, and he was very heavy-handed. Since then, I've been unimpressed and completely unhappy. I kept asking when the orthodontics would be finished. The doctor would tell me to wait until the teeth were properly pulled in, sometimes pulling them further apart, then pulling them closer together again. I kept trying until I finally couldn't take it anymore. I asked the doctor when it would be finished, and he said about six or seven months. I'm praying for it to be finished soon, so I'm going to move on to another procedure. I'm really unhappy with the doctor.

Many times, the doctor's words shouldn't have come out of his mouth. For example, "You've come a long way since you started." I haven't had my wisdom teeth extracted, and he said, "Eventually, I'll have to have them extracted." I haven't had my implants installed, and he said, "Eventually, all my teeth will fall out." Shouldn't these words have come out of his mouth? And most importantly, he's incredibly heavy-handed. I don't know if he's heavy-handed with everyone or just me.

If he continues to be like this, I'll probably go somewhere else after I get my braces done. The scheduling process is terrible. Sometimes I wait for half an hour, and he just says he's busy, so why should I schedule an appointment?

The doctor told me he gave me the best advice. I'm not trying to say he knows better than the doctor, but I don't think his advice was the best.

If I improve, I'll come back and update my review. Dr. P.

The staff were confused about scheduling, for example, "Are you available on Saturday or Sunday?"
Me: "Okay."
Staff: "The orthodontist comes in every other week, but won't be coming in the following week. Are you available Monday to Friday?"
Me: "Monday to Friday is the doctor's schedule?"
Staff: "The orthodontist can put on the braces."
Me: "The doctor referred me to an orthodontist for a consultation and to proceed with the next steps. Please read what the doctor says first."
Staff: "But the doctor won't be coming in next week."
Me (thinking to myself): "Then why would I come Monday to Friday to get braces put on? We haven't even started yet! I'm so confused."
Me: "That's okay. I'll schedule another appointment when I have the chance."

Actually, I asked many more questions than that.
All I could do was say "It's okay," and tell them to change appointments. It's a waste of time.
